citation: de Morais Junior AC, Schincaglia RM, Passarelli M, et al. Acute Epigallocatechin-3-Gallate Supplementation Alters Postprandial Lipids after a Fast-Food Meal in Healthy Young Women: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Crossover Study. Nutrients. 2020;12(9):2533.
protocol: Fast-food meal (McDonald's fries 80 g, bacon 130 g and other items; 1027 kcal: 20.57 g carbohydrate, 47.41 g protein, 83.90 g fat of which 37.17 g saturated) taken after capsules of 800 mg EGCG or placebo; crossover. Blood at 0, 90, 120 min after the end of the meal.
population: 14 healthy young women, 21 ± 1 y, BMI 21.4 ± 0.41 kg/m2; Brazil (Goiás).

reports.where: Table 2: response (time points/AUC) for placebo and EGCG

note: A very fat- and protein-rich, low-carbohydrate real meal in lean young women; use the placebo arm. Sampling is sparse (90 and 120 min only), so the peak is missed. Meal kinds: fat load, mixed meal.
